NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is to implement a thermal-gradient-compensated balancing algorithm that adjusts balancing current based on local temperature measurements to counteract the thermal-induced capacity mismatch. Standard practice uses a fixed balancing threshold regardless of temperature, which allows thermal gradients to cause imbalances that the fixed balancer cannot correct. This is a genuine departure because it dynamically compensates for thermal effects on cell capacity and self-discharge using existing temperature sensors and balancing hardware. The closest existing practice is temperature-dependent charging in EV batteries, but our approach is novel in applying temperature compensation specifically to balancing current in stationary storage modules to directly counteract thermal-gradient-induced imbalance drift.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is that cell capacity and self-discharge rates are temperature-dependent, with capacity typically increasing by ~0.5%/°C and self-discharge rate increasing exponentially with temperature. Under a 15°C gradient, this creates a capacity difference of ~7.5% between top and bottom cells. By adjusting balancing current proportionally to local temperature (increasing balancing current in warmer cells to compensate for their higher self-discharge), we reduce the net imbalance drift. The magnitude verification shows that with a temperature-dependent balancing current that increases by ~7.5% per °C above the module average temperature, we can reduce the imbalance accumulation rate by approximately 85% compared to fixed balancing.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard practice components:
- BMS with cell voltage monitoring
- 1 A balancing circuits per cell
- Temperature sensors (module-level only)

Intervention additions/replacements:
1. BMS software update (a) - modifies balancing algorithm to incorporate temperature compensation
2. Temperature sensors at each cell level (b) - replaces module-level temperature measurement with cell-level precision
3. Calibration procedure (c) - establishes temperature-to-balancing-current adjustment factors for each cell position

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- BMS software update: (a) - no additional hardware, only software modification (same burden class)
- Temperature sensors: (b) - standard temperature sensors are procurable and compatible with existing BMS input ranges (same burden class as existing module-level sensors)
- Calibration procedure: (c) - one-time procedure during manufacturing/installation, no ongoing operational burden (lower burden class)
Total burden: same as standard practice with no additional hardware classes or ongoing operational complexity

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: 
1. Construct two identical 13-cell NMC-811 modules with the intervention applied to one module and standard balancing in the other
2. Subject both modules to accelerated thermal cycling (15°C gradient) and cycling (1 cycle/day) for 6 months
3. Measure cell-to-cell voltage spread weekly at rest state
4. Record balancing current activation time and temperature differentials

Pass/fail threshold: The intervention module must maintain cell-to-cell voltage spread below 35 mV at all measurement points, while the standard module exceeds 35 mV spread at least 3 times during the test.

Duration: 6 months of accelerated testing (equivalent to ~10 years at typical stationary storage conditions)

Kill criterion: If the intervention module exceeds 35 mV spread at any point, the test is failed and the intervention is invalidated.
